Return {"pieces":[{"piece_id":"01","markdown":"...","claim_ids":[...]}]} for each supplied brief. Write 600–900 English words EXCLUDING references per article. Include the actual as-of date. Develop the brief's distinct argument, cross-source reasoning, uncertainty and limitation. Preserve every claim marker [01-c1] etc adjacent to supporting discussion. Use all and only brief claims. Cite provided evidence with readable source labels/URLs and timestamps. Clearly distinguish source claims and your interpretation. No new factual assertions without evidence. No fabricated personal tests. References appended by the pipeline do not count toward word target.

Keep assignment logistics, pipeline implementation details, student approval and policy-revision status out of audience-facing briefs/articles/narration. Those belong in submission and review documentation.
Do not generate a separate reference appendix: the pipeline appends canonical readable references. Keep inline citations and all claim markers.

Write all generated editorial prose and explanations in English. Preserve original source quotations, proper names, IDs, and timestamp locators exactly.

GitHub's incident report supplies a counterweight: a completed job did not necessarily deliver a review. Together, these sources suggest that the meaningful change is a broader set of development actions, while the reader's acceptance criterion should remain an inspectable result rather than an agent's completion signal. This reasoning is captured in 01-c5.", "limitations": "Cursor and GitHub describe products they sell, and GitHub reports its own incident and mitigation. Willison reports on his own application without a controlled comparison or complete testing and correction costs. Cursor Security Review requires Teams or Enterprise access; individual purchase practicality remains unresolved. An experienced maintainer's profiling experiment does not establish that a developer with basic skills can reproduce it without additional setup and interpretation. These sources provide neither independent research on solo-project completion nor representative evidence from first-time users, abandoned projects or accessibility users.", "claims": [{"claim_id": "01-c1", "statement": "Cursor announced that its iOS app can display and message local agents. Benchmark design, developer response and second-model criticism each answer different questions.", "synthesis": "GitHub's ReviewBench offers inspectable tasks and an explicit account of its metrics, but deliberately reduces tiny changes and uses an LLM to judge whether comments prompted edits. Cursor promises actionable security findings, while Willison reports trying adversarial review without establishing its effectiveness. These are complementary signals, not independent confirmation of successful delivery: a comment can prompt a change without proving the change was necessary or correct. The resulting distinction is expressed in 02-c5.", "limitations": "GitHub built the benchmark with Microsoft and evaluates a product it sells; its separate relabeling exercise used internal senior engineers rather than an independent publisher. The combined implication in 03-c5 is to measure verified task completion, including human correction, rather than generation alone.", "limitations": "These are proposed checks, not tests performed for this brief.
